header.running_head: Occupation with the Ahadeeth of Rasulullaah ﷺ and Befitting Behaviour for those Occupied with this

blocks.text: Imaam emerged to lead the salaah. He then sat down. [^1]
The Difficulty Hadhrat Umar (RA), Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) and Hadhrat Ali (RA) Experienced Narrating Ahadeeth

Hadhrat Aslam reports that when they used to ask Hadhrat Umar (RA) to narrate Ahadeeth to them, he would say, "I fear that I may add a word or omit a word because Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'The person who intentionally lies about me is headed for Jahannam." [^2]

Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Haatib says, "I have not seen any of the Sahabah (RA) narrate Ahadeeth as well and as thoroughly as Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA). However, he was a man who was extremely reluctant to narrate Ahadeeth." [^3]

Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) used to say, "What prevents me from narrating Ahadeeth from Rasulullaah ﷺ is not the fact that I was not one of those Sahabah (RA) with the best memories. What prevents me is that I can testify that I heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, 'Whoever attributes anything to me that I never stated should prepare for his abode in Jahannam.'" Another narration quotes Rasulullaah ﷺ's words as, "Whoever speaks lies about me should prepare for a house in Jahannam." [^4]

Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "When narrating Ahadeeth to you, I prefer falling from the sky rather than stating something that Rasulullaah ﷺ never said. However, when speaking to you about matters between us, then (precautions need not be so strict because) wars are won by strategy." [^5]
The Difficulty Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) Experienced with Narrating Ahadeeth

Hadhrat Amr bin Maymoon reports that sometimes an entire year would pass by without Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) narrating a single Hadith. When he narrated a Hadith one day, he started to shiver and perspiration beaded up on his forehead. He then said, "Rasulullaah ﷺ said something like that or stated similar words." [^6]

Hadhrat Masrooq reports, "Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) started to narrate a Hadith one day, but as soon as he said, 'Rasulullaah ﷺ said,' he started to shiver so much that even his clothing shook. He then added, 'Rasulullaah ﷺ said something to the effect or something similar.'" [^7]
Haakim, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Dhahabi.
Ahmad, Ibn Adi, Uqayli and Abu Nu'aym in his Ma'rifah, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.239).
Ibn Sa'd and Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.9).
Ahmad, Abu Ya'la and Bazzaar. Haythami (Vol.1 Pg.143) has commented on the chain of narrators.
Bukhaari, Muslim and others, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.240).
Haakim (Vol.3 Pg.314), reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Dhahabi.
Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami (Vol.1 Pg.79). Isaabah (Vol.3 Pg.156) has reported a similar narration.
